title: How votes are counted after an election
examples: What happens at an election count?

stages.label: Polls close
stages.note: Ballot boxes are sealed in front of witnesses.
stages.ask: Why are ballot boxes sealed?

stages.label: Boxes to the count
stages.note: Officials carry sealed boxes to a counting hall.

stages.label: Check the totals
stages.note: Papers are counted to match the number given out.
stages.ask: Why do they check the number of ballot papers?

stages.label: Sort by candidate
stages.note: Papers are sorted into piles, one per candidate.
stages.ask: What is a spoiled ballot?

stages.label: Count in bundles
stages.note: Bundles of, say, 25 or 50 are counted and checked.
stages.ask: Who watches the votes being counted?

stages.label: Result declared
stages.note: The official announces each candidate's votes.
stages.ask: What happens if the result is very close?

explain.say: On election day, millions of people mark a paper with their choice. But how do those papers become a result by the next morning? Look at the first stage. When voting ends, the ballot boxes are sealed shut in front of witnesses, so nobody can add or remove a paper.

explain.say: The sealed boxes travel to a counting hall. Now see the scale? Officials open each box and count the papers, to check they match the number handed out at that polling station. Why do you think that check matters?

explain.say: Yes, it shows nothing went missing or was added! Look at the next stage. Counters sort the papers into piles, one for each candidate. Papers that are blank or unclear are put aside for the official in charge to decide.

faq.a: Sealing the boxes, with witnesses watching, makes sure nobody can add, remove or change any ballot papers between voting and counting.
asks: How are ballot boxes kept safe?

faq.q: Why do they check the number of ballot papers?
faq.a: Matching the papers in each box with the number given out at that polling station shows that none went missing or were added.
asks: How do they know no votes are lost?

faq.q: Who watches the votes being counted?
faq.a: Agents for each candidate and party, and often independent observers, watch closely so the count is open and fair.
asks: Can anyone watch an election count?

faq.q: What happens if the result is very close?
faq.a: Candidates can ask for a recount, where the papers are counted again. In an exact tie, rules in some places decide by drawing lots.
A ballot paper that can't be counted, for example because it is blank, marked for too many candidates, or the choice isn't clear.
asks: What happens to unclear ballot papers?

facts: In many countries, agents for every candidate may watch paper ballots being counted.
In the UK, a tied election result is settled by drawing lots.
